key_insight: Multiscale simulations identify a dynamically stabilized hexagonal ZrO interlayer that shapes columnar oxide grains and impedes oxygen diffusion during zirconium corrosion.
engineering_relevance: The model links oxide microstructure, oxygen transport, and local tensile stresses to mechanisms relevant to zirconium corrosion resistance and crack initiation.
method: Compute ZrOₓ properties using first-principles density functional theory.
Use a DFT-trained machine-learned potential for molecular dynamics inputs.
Model oxide growth with multiphase phase fields coupling nucleation, diffusion, anisotropic elasticity, and phase stability.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports reproduction of columnar oxide morphology and grain-size distributions observed in micrographs, along with an undulatory metal/oxide interface.
watch_item: The abstract provides no quantitative validation errors, and the proposed link between the ZrO barrier and sub-parabolic corrosion kinetics remains tentative.
paper_title: Multiscale Modeling of Zr Corrosion: Predicting Microstructures of Oxide Films
